title: Tortellini in Brodo
subtitle: Pork and Parmesan stuffed pasta in clear beef and chicken broth
excerpt: Tortellini in brodo is the essential Christmas dish of Bologna: small, ring-shaped pasta stuffed with pork loin, prosciutto, mortadella, Parmesan, and nutmeg, served in a clear, deeply flavoured broth of beef and chicken. The tortellini and the broth are both made from scratch and both require time. It is the dish Bolognesi argue about most.
sourceNotes: Tortellini in brodo is the traditional Christmas dish of Bologna and is codified by the Confraternita del Tortellino, who deposited the original recipe with the Bologna Chamber of Commerce in 1974. The recipe uses beef or capon broth. Filling: pork loin, prosciutto crudo, mortadella, Parmesan, nutmeg, egg.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the uncooked tortellini on a tray, then transfer to a bag. Cook from frozen in simmering broth for 4 to 5 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double quantity of filling and freeze in portions. The broth also freezes well.

glossaryTerms.definition: Small ring-shaped stuffed pasta from Bologna and Modena, traditionally filled with pork, prosciutto, mortadella, Parmesan, and nutmeg, and served in clear beef or capon broth. According to Bolognese legend, the shape was inspired by the navel of the goddess Venus.

content.text: in brodo is a two-day project in most Bolognese households: the broth simmers on day one, the filling is made and refrigerated overnight, and the pasta is rolled and the tortellini formed on day two. The filling must be cold to be pliable. The broth must be clear: skim it frequently and never let it boil.

Place {{beef-brisket}} of beef brisket, {{chicken-whole}} chicken, {{carrot}} carrots, {{celery}} celery sticks, {{onion}} halved onion, and {{salt-table}} salt in a large pot. Cover with 3 litres of cold water. Bring slowly to a gentle simmer over 30 minutes, skimming any foam. Cook at the lowest possible simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours. The broth should never boil properly. Strain through a fine sieve, discard the solids, and refrigerate. Skim the solidified fat from the top the next day.

Briefly pan-fry {{pork-loin}} of pork loin in a dry pan until just cooked through. Cool completely, then finely mince together with {{prosciutto}} of prosciutto and the mortadella or extra prosciutto by pulsing in a food processor. Transfer to a bowl and mix in {{parmesan}} of grated Parmesan, {{eggs}} egg, and {{nutmeg}} of nutmeg. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour (overnight is better).
Make the pasta and form the tortellini

Mound {{00-flour}} of 00 flour on a clean surface. Make a well in the centre and crack in {{eggs}} eggs. Beat the eggs with a fork, gradually incorporating the flour. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and silky. Wrap in cling film and rest for 30 minutes.

Roll the pasta very thin using a pasta machine -- to setting 6 or 7 out of 9, almost transparent. Cut into 4 cm squares. Place a tiny amount of filling (about 0.5 tsp) in the centre of each square. Fold the square diagonally to form a triangle, pressing the edges to seal. Bring the two long corners of the triangle together around your finger and press firmly to seal. They should look like small rings. Place on a lightly floured tray.

Bring the broth to a gentle simmer. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Add the tortellini and cook for 3 minutes until the pasta is just tender. Serve in warmed bowls with a generous ladle of broth and a dusting of Parmesan at the table.

items.symptom: The tortellini come unstuck during cooking
items.cause: The edges were not sealed firmly, or the pasta had dried out and would not stick.
items.fix: Press the edges of the pasta firmly and dampen them with a little water if the pasta has dried. Work quickly once the pasta is rolled.

items.cause: It boiled rather than simmering gently, or was not skimmed during cooking.
items.fix: A clear broth requires a very gentle simmer throughout. Skim frequently in the first 30 minutes. A cloudy broth tastes the same but is not traditional.

content.text: Tortellini in brodo is the most argued-over dish in Bologna. In 1974, the Confraternita del Tortellino lodged the original recipe with the Bologna Chamber of Commerce to fix the formula. The group still runs competitions and trains pasta makers. The dish appears on Christmas Eve and Christmas Day in most Bolognese homes. In Bologna, the quality of a family's tortellini is a source of serious pride. One rule is firm: the filling goes through the mincer before cooking, not after, and must rest overnight.
